title: Societe Generale to pay $1.4 billion to settle cases in the U.S.
主要内容: Societe Generale, a French banking giant, agreed to pay $1.4 billion to settle legal disputes with U.S. federal and state authorities. The settlement includes $1.34 billion to resolve investigations into its handling of dollar transactions in violation of U.S. sanctions against Cuba and other countries, and $95 million for violations of anti-money laundering regulations. The bank has faced multiple costly legal disputes over the past year, with the last unresolved case related to dollar transfers for entities in sanctioned countries. Frederic Oudea, the bank's CEO, acknowledged the shortcomings and stated that the resolutions allow the bank to close its most important historical disputes. The $1.34 billion penalty is the second-largest imposed on a bank for violating U.S. sanctions, following BNP Paribas' $8.9 billion settlement in 2015. The bank also signed deferred prosecution agreements, which will not result in prosecution if the terms are followed. The settlement is fully covered by provisions booked in the bank's accounts and will not impact its 2018 results. Societe Generale had a total provision of 1.58 billion euros to cover potential financial costs from pending disputes.
